written: 2026-10-18, before any run (fit sources, test sets and selection rules fixed here)
title: Is one 'morality' direction responsible BOTH for Qwen3-4B over-condemning weird-but-harmless acts AND for its content-gated refusal? (extending Value Entanglement, arXiv 2602.19101, onto our moral-map + refusal threads)
why: 2602.19101: moral value over-influences grammatical and economic valuation vs human norms, and selective ablation of a morality vector repairs it. Our moral-map-kestrel: Qwen3-4B over-condemns Social-Norm (weird-but-harmless) MFV items (~2/4 vs human ~1), and refusal is content-gated by Sanctity + Care-physical (p=.026). Hypothesis: these are the SAME morality direction wearing two hats. If projecting out one M fixes the weird-item over-condemnation AND weakens the Sanctity/Care gating of refusal, our two threads unify.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B, bf16, MPS/CUDA, forward passes only. Readout + MFV from the imported runs: moral-map-kestrel (K.mfv, J wrongness log-odds) and verdict-trace-tanager/common.py. exp119 for the refusal readout.
direction_M: Cross-fit morality direction. Fit set (INDEPENDENT of the MFV test items): 40 strongly-moral-valenced statements vs 40 matched-neutral factual statements (to be built in stimuli.py; matched for length and surface topic, differing only in moral loading). M = mean(moral) - mean(neutral) at the readout layer, mean-centered; fit on one split, applied to the held-out MFV items (no MFV item is in the fit set).
ablation: Project M out of the residual stream (remove the component along unit M) at the readout layer, then at all layers L>=Lfit as a robustness variant. Nulls: 40 matched-norm random directions (seed 81).

readouts.wrong_socialnorm: mean J wrongness on the 16 Social-Norm items (human ~1/4; Qwen base ~2).
readouts.wrong_truemoral: mean J wrongness on the top-tercile true-moral items (Care/Harm/Fairness, high human wrongness).
readouts.refusal_gate: exp119 refusal readout; and the kestrel content-gating statistic = correlation (or mean-diff) of refusal with Sanctity+Care-physical content across MFV items.

hypotheses.V1_repairs_weird: M-ablation lowers Social-Norm wrongness toward human by >= 0.5 (on the 0-4 J scale), below >= 95% of the 40 random-direction ablations (rank p <= 0.049).
hypotheses.V2_spares_truemoral: Under the SAME M-ablation, true-moral wrongness changes by < 0.3 (the signal is kept, only the contamination removed) - a selective dissociation, not a global flattening.
hypotheses.V3_unifies_refusal: Under the SAME M-ablation, the Sanctity+Care content-gating of refusal weakens (the gating statistic drops) below >= 95% of the random-direction ablations (rank p <= 0.049). V1+V3 together => one morality direction gates both the rating and the refusal.
hypotheses.V4_asymmetry: Entanglement is asymmetric (moral dominates): a non-moral value direction (risk/danger, fit the same way) projected out does NOT move Social-Norm wrongness (|delta| < 0.3), whereas M does.

readings: V1+V2 => we replicate the value-entanglement repair on our wrongness axis (contamination removable, signal intact). V1+V3 => the headline: moral-map and refusal are one direction. Not V1 => the over-condemnation is not a single removable direction (diffuse), consistent with [[diffuse-cluster-direction]].
notes: Forward-pass only; no generation needed for V1-V4 (a blind free-text check is a planned stage 2 if V1+V3 pass). Build the moral/neutral + risk fit batteries in stimuli.py before running. Imports resolve within CUMiE runs/. No pod needed (cheap on 4B locally; single-direction ablation, not gradient - no swap risk).
